title: CS & Sales Enterprise Asks: Aggregation, Initial Scoping, and Handoff Protocol
creator: Ethan Rivera
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success frequently surface non-bug enterprise feature requests with inconsistent context, unclear business impact, and no standard first-pass scoping. This slows product decisions and increases back-and-forth with customers.

Goal: Create a lightweight, repeatable protocol and artifacts that allow CS/Sales to submit enterprise asks with the minimum set of fields for prioritization, produce an initial product/engineering scoping estimate, and drive a clear handoff outcome (Accept->Roadmap/Backlog, Investigate, Defer, Decline). Reduce time-to-triage and improve predictability for enterprise deals.

Scope: covers feature requests (non-bug), proof-of-concept asks, compliance/enterprise controls requested through Sales/CS. Excludes security vulnerabilities, outage incidents, and legal contract negotiations (handled by Security/Legal).

Deliverables:
- A standardized submission template (Salesforce/Gainsight + Slack shortcut) capturing customer, use case, expected value, data residency/security constraints, rough scale, and desired timeline.
- A lightweight scoring rubric (Impact, Strategic Fit, Implementation Effort, Risk) with guidance and numeric thresholds.
- A templated initial scoping worksheet for PM/Eng to estimate effort (S/M/L) and high-level technical risks.
- A follow-up sequence and SLA: initial triage within 5 business days, scoping estimate within 10 business days, and clear handoff outcome.
- A single Linear board view / label convention to track enterprise ask lifecycle and enable reporting (time to triage, backlog conversion rate).
acceptance_criteria: Submission template added to Salesforce and accessible via a short link; checklist of required fields enforced
Scoring rubric documented in Confluence with worked examples for 3 recent customer asks
PM/Eng scoping template exists and has been used to produce 3 test scoping estimates with engineering sign-off
SLA defined and tested: 5-business-day triage and 10-business-day scoping for requests that pass the initial gate
Linear board / labels created and 2-week reporting dashboard showing triage time and conversion metrics

2026-03-12 | CS (Alicia Gomez): Agreed to pilot by training two AE reps and adding the template to the customer intake playbook. Will provide 3 example historical asks to use for rubric calibration.

2026-03-13 | PM (Maya Chen): Updated rubric to include 'regulatory risk' as a separate dimension after legal flagged compliance gravity. Draft scoring doc: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1abc-example

2026-03-13 | Decision: Keep intake lightweight. Trade-off: fewer initial fields -> faster submissions but higher probability of follow-up. Mitigation: require specific redlines for compliance and private deployment flags to gate requests.
